1.why: At fixed Q = A × v, a smaller wet area requires a higher average water speed.

wrong.a: Water still flows because discharge stays nonzero.
wrong.c: Slower water through a smaller area would reduce discharge.
wrong.d: At the same speed, a smaller area would reduce discharge.

2.why: Q is the volume of water passing a cross-section per second.

wrong.b: Temperature measures hotness, not volume per second.
wrong.c: River length is a distance, not volume per second.
wrong.d: Air pressure is not a volume flow rate.

3.why: Absorbent ground lets some rain soak into soil, reducing rapid surface runoff.

wrong.a: Narrowing riverbanks does not help soil absorb rainfall.
wrong.b: Waste can block drains; it does not help rain soak into soil.
wrong.d: Paving covers soil and reduces water absorption.

_quiz_pool.question: What does Q stand for in river water flow?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Q is volumetric flow rate, volume passing per second.

_quiz_pool.question: At fixed discharge, if cross-section area A decreases, velocity v must...
_quiz_pool.explanation: By continuity (Q = A × v), smaller area means higher speed.

_quiz_pool.question: What is the unit of volumetric flow rate Q?
Why do heavy rains cause river water levels to rise quickly?
options: Runoff enters faster than water drains
_quiz_pool.explanation: Heavy rain creates rapid surface runoff into rivers.

_quiz_pool.question: What does A represent in the river flow equation?
_quiz_pool.explanation: A is the cross-sectional area of the channel.

_quiz_pool.question: Which measure helps reduce urban flood peaks?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Retention ponds store peak water and slow down flow.

_quiz_pool.question: If A = 10 m² and v = 2 m/s, what is Q?
What agencies monitor rainfall and floods in Indonesia?
_quiz_pool.explanation: BMKG monitors weather and BNPB manages disaster response.

_quiz_pool.question: At fixed discharge, what happens to speed when the wet area increases?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Larger area means slower flow for the same discharge Q.

_quiz_pool.question: For steady incompressible flow with no side inflow, continuity means...
_quiz_pool.explanation: Volume flow rate remains constant along the channel.

story.title: Rain warnings and river flow
story.lead: BMKG warned of heavy rain across parts of Indonesia in its November outlook. Bengkulu, Aceh and West Sumatra recorded high daily rainfall [1].
story.image_caption: Ciliwung headwaters at Telaga Warna (archive photo).
stat.1.label: Bengkulu daily rain in the observed period [1]
stat.2.label: Aceh daily rain in the observed period [1]
stat.3.label: West Sumatra daily rain in the observed period [1]
story.body_1: Rain reaching the ground can soak into soil or flow downhill as runoff. Some runoff enters streams and rivers, carrying water toward the sea [2]. More incoming water can change river flow, so a rain warning is a reason to pay attention to local conditions.
story.body_2: Scientists measure a river channel and its average water speed to work out discharge: the volume passing each second [3]. Our classroom example uses chosen values, not measurements of an Indonesian river.
timeline.1.text: Heavy daily rain was recorded in several regions [1].
timeline.2.text: BMKG warned of more heavy rain in parts of Indonesia [1].
timeline.3.text: Follow local warnings and observe conditions safely.
physics.title: Water flow and continuity
physics.body_1: How much water moves through a river per second is called discharge, Q. It depends on the cross-section area A and the speed of the water v.
physics.body_2: For steady flow with no side inflow, discharge stays constant along a channel. A smaller wet cross-section then requires a higher average speed.
physics.assumptions: Chosen classroom values, not field data. Steady flow; no side inflow, compression or storage changes.
